properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-30, on noticing a pattern in agent replies: a number is announced ("59 undeclared boundaries"), and only afterwards comes "here is what I actually measured". He asked whether the ordering can be switched, and whether that is a reflow2 change or an agent tendency.

MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and it is BOTH — but the reflow2 half is specific and fixable:

`seam_coverage` emits a scope_note that says, in words, that a design declaring its contracts at a HIGHER boundary than it records its dependencies will read as having none at module level, and tells the caller to pass `altitude`. That warning is correct and it is right there in the tool.

`maturity_report`'s seams band asks the SAME question — "Of the couplings between two Components, how many run through a declared Interface that one provides and the other consumes?", population 72, present 13 — at module level, with NO altitude and NONE of that warning. `graph_report_markdown` then prints `seams 18% (13/72) ← frontier`, barer still. Its `not_observed_about` list is long and careful and does not include the one caveat its sibling tool considers essential.

⭐ SO THE CAVEAT EXISTS AND IS STRIPPED BY THE TOOL THAT QUOTES THE NUMBER. That is not an agent tendency. An agent reading the trajectory band has nothing to be suspicious of, and 18% was in fact wrong twice over (dec fix on 2026-08-30: the roll-up dropped 58 of 86 modules; the honest reading is 13 of 19 at subsystem altitude, six boundaries genuinely undeclared).

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:

(a) A band carries the population caveat of whatever computed it — the note travels with the number rather than living only at its source. Root fix, matches "an id prefix carries no meaning a computation may read" in spirit: a NUMBER carries no meaning without its population. Cost: every report grows, and reports are already long.

(b) Bands distinguish a STRONG number from a WEAK one. "Delivered 153 of 194" is strong — the thread is real and each hop is an edge somebody drew. "Seams 18%" is weak — the two vocabularies do not meet by construction, which the design already recorded as fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet. Nothing in the report tells a reader which kind of number they are holding. Cost: "strong/weak" is a judgement, and dec:report-dont-judge says reflow2 reports and does not rule.

(c) The maturity seams band is answered AT ALTITUDE, or states that it is module-level. Narrowest fix, addresses this instance and not the class.

(d) A skill instruction: where-am-i must re-derive a band from its source tool before naming it the FRONTIER, because the frontier is the one band that drives what the user does next. Targeted rather than "measure everything". Cost: it is an instruction with no detector behind it, which is the weakest of the three legs (fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it), and where-am-i is meant to be a cheap check-in.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO THE USER'S ASK AS STATED: "measure first, then report" applied generally would make orientation expensive — where-am-i would have to run the tool behind every band on every check-in. The cheaper shape is that a number arrives WITH what it was computed over, so a reader can see which ones are weak, and the agent goes and measures only the one that is about to drive a decision.
properties.name: OPEN — should a derived number carry its own caveat wherever it is quoted, so a warning cannot be stripped by the tool that repeats the number?
properties.rationale: Recorded so the pattern Anthony noticed is not lost as a conversational remark. The measurement behind it — that seam_coverage's scope_note is stripped by maturity_report and graph_report_markdown asking the same question without it — is the part that makes this a reflow2 question rather than a prompt-engineering one.
